correctness.rationale: Kayacan's criterion reduces ordinary domination to covering every minimal subgroup. In exponent \(p\), every nonidentity element has order \(p\), so maximal-subgroup replacement converts the problem to covering \(V=G/Z(G)\cong\mathbb F_p^{2n}\) by hyperplanes. At most \(p\) hyperplanes cannot cover \(V\), while the \(p+1\) hyperplanes through a codimension-two subspace do; their lifts all contain \(Z(G)\), hence form a clique, and \(p+1\) is even. In exponent \(p^2\), odd-prime class-two collection gives \((xy)^p=x^py^p\); the nonzero homomorphism \(x\mapsto x^p\) maps onto the order-\(p\) center, so its index-\(p\) kernel contains every order-\(p\) subgroup and dominates alone. Pairing that kernel with \(Z(G)\) gives sharp total and paired value \(2\).
correctness.risk: The odd-prime power-map argument does not apply to extraspecial \(2\)-groups, where quadratic-form structure intervenes.
